$comment: Context graph of the w bundle. Single source for BOTH measurement (aw context-budget) and resolution (aw context-plan). It lives inside the bundle on purpose: a hand-installed tree carries the manifest that describes IT, so a receipt can never describe a bundle other than the one the agent actually reads. Paths are relative to the bundle root. `core` is loaded always, in order; a module is loaded only when its signal is observed.

signals.plan-mode: the host reports it is planning, so the command describes instead of acting
signals.adopted: the conversation already produced the analysis, plan or answers the run needs
signals.probe: the run rests on a runnable assumption that reading cannot settle
signals.db: the run reads or writes a database
signals.ui: the run produces or changes a user interface
signals.split: the deliverable may have to become more than one document
signals.shape: the investigation may have changed what kind of document this is
signals.input: the argument is not plainly the document this command expects
signals.resume: a prior run over this same input may exist
signals.replan: work already executed has to be re-planned around
signals.simulation: the change carries temporary behavior with a boundary to declare
signals.compaction: the run is long enough that context pressure governs its pacing
signals.sessions: a session other than this run's own has to be located, named or reopened
signals.web: the run needs evidence from outside the workspace
signals.reconnaissance: a draft is being cut from a raw prompt over unfamiliar terrain
signals.detection: the CLI's automatic detection was wrong or ambiguous
signals.scaffold: the target has materialized runtime or needs its materialization/configuration contract
signals.classification: in-conversation work has to be classified before it is written
signals.authoring: the deliverable's own notation, structure or ordering is not obvious from the material
signals.route: the flow is at its adaptive route evaluation boundary

$comment_flow_signals: Vocabulary the AGENT may declare at a flow boundary — kept HERE, next to the context signals, so there is one catalog and not two that drift. The frontier is exact: recognizing a signal is judgment (the agent's), applying the threshold over the declared signals is a rule (the CLI's). A signal outside this vocabulary never advances a journey. Each id must be consumed by some transition of the authority registry, and every signal a transition consumes must appear here: the guard runs in both directions.

flow_signals.quick.needs-architecture: the objective cannot be met without deciding how responsibilities are distributed
flow_signals.quick.two-or-more-sources: the change reaches two or more declared sources
flow_signals.quick.multiple-deliverables: the objective bundles more than one independent deliverable
flow_signals.quick.large-feature-or-refactor: the size is that of a feature or a refactor, not a scoped fix
flow_signals.quick.ambiguous-requirements: what is being asked needs elicitation before anything can be built
flow_signals.quick.deliverable-is-analysis: what the task produces is an analysis or a design, so its criterion is a rubric a person ratifies
flow_signals.spec.functional-ambiguity: a functional ambiguity with two readings that would change what gets built is blocking this spec
flow_signals.spec.solution-space-unexplored: a trigger of the ideation gate fires: the spec settled on its first idea and the alternatives would change the outcome
flow_signals.spec.escalation-adopted: this refine consumed the escalation package an execution handed over, instead of re-deriving its diagnosis
flow_signals.spec.escalation-absent: no escalation package reached this refine, so it starts from the spec alone
flow_signals.spec.independent-outcomes: the prompt holds outcomes each worth delivering on its own
flow_signals.spec.enumerated-features: the prompt enumerates distinct features explicitly
flow_signals.spec.distinct-moments: the parts are requested for different moments or in a stated order
flow_signals.spec.independent-value: the users or the value of each part do not depend on the others
flow_signals.plan.independent-tranches: the tranches are executable and deliverable independently
flow_signals.plan.no-shared-deps: the tranches share neither dependencies nor risk
flow_signals.plan.distinct-priorities: the tranches are requested at different moments or priorities
flow_signals.plan.far-beyond-s: the plan far exceeds S-complexity phases
flow_signals.plan.staging-requested: the person asked for the work to be staged
flow_signals.plan.dependency-outside-range: a phase of the range depends on something neither already satisfied nor an earlier phase of that same range
flow_signals.plan.result-shapes-later: a phase result, proof, probe or human decision determines how a later phase has to be built
flow_signals.plan.blocker-between-phases: an unresolved question, a live blocker, an operative handoff or an irreversible external action sits between the phases
flow_signals.plan.recovery-boundary: an intermediate commit, release, review or deployment is a required recovery boundary
flow_signals.plan.not-one-reviewable-unit: the combined change is not coherent, recoverable and reviewable as a single unit
flow_signals.plan.entry-gap-minor: the plan is all but executable: the gap is derivable from what it already states, so it can be normalized in place
flow_signals.plan.entry-gap-structural: phases, contracts or journey are missing, or temporary behavior leaves its boundary undeclared
flow_signals.plan.deviation-structural: the change that appeared while implementing touches a contract, the participating components, the phase order or the simulation boundary
flow_signals.plan.deviation-functional: the change that appeared while implementing moves the promise of the product: the expected result, the functional scope, a business rule, the actor, or the outcome an acceptance criterion states
flow_signals.plan.deviation-composable: the change keeps the functional lineage and can be reconciled forward as a durable decision note instead of returning to a refine
flow_signals.plan.deviation-escalation: what was found does not compose against this lineage and belongs to a spec of its own
flow_signals.plan.closure-lineage: the divergence stays inside the same functional lineage: it amends how the promise is met, not who promised it
flow_signals.plan.closure-intent: the intent behind the divergence is settled, so nothing further has to be elicited before deciding
flow_signals.plan.closure-impact: the transitive impact can be enumerated: every consumer the decision reaches is nameable
flow_signals.plan.closure-recoverable: the result can be sealed and recovered: an identical retry gives the same outcome and a failure leaves nothing half-written
flow_signals.plan.escalation-adopted: this refine consumed the escalation package an execution handed over, instead of re-deriving its diagnosis
flow_signals.plan.escalation-absent: no escalation package reached this refine, so it starts from the document alone
flow_signals.chassis.context-pressure: a fresh reader would need the CHECKPOINT to continue this run
flow_signals.quick.db-touched: the task read from or wrote to a database, so there is a statement to derive into the session script

capabilities.$comment: Conformant capabilities: the same read-set question as a command, and deliberately NOT commands — no commands/<name>.md, no activation median, no reclassification as a single-pass command.

budget_policy.$comment: Ratios of the frozen baseline (spec 009 § Decisions: -30% discovery, -40% median and -20% minimum activation, -25% median execution, +5% ceiling per journey). Absolute targets are DERIVED from baseline x ratio, never written by hand. The +5% ceiling also caps modules.total, the conditional tree as one figure: a representative journey carries no signal, so no journey line ever prices a module, and without that line the modules would grow unwatched.
